summary: Wrote src\en\module_05\12-concepts-c.md: concept sections s9 PINNs (1903 words / target 1700), s10 neural operators (952 / 850), s11 contrastive learning (1064 / 1050), s12 mixture of experts (950 / 850), s13 choosing a family (690 / 650), all within +/-15%, total 5559 concept words, plus 'What goes wrong' {#wrong} with all 13 plan items as symptom/cause/fix under ### headings (1079 words). Every must_cover item, all 9 planned worked examples (as ::: worked boxes with arithmetic written out), figures fig-05-21 to fig-05-29 with precise captions, and all 9 planned checks with answers are in place. The section has no widget. Every number was recomputed (labpy.sh): the near-miss residual 0.8 pi^2 = 7.90, mean r^2 31.17 (31.02 on 200 points), the non-dimensional 0.02, InfoNCE 0.810/0.577 and 0.0013/1.385, log 256 = 5.55, log 511 = 6.24, the Mixtral counts 176.2M/45.1B/41.9M/1.34B/0.26B/46.7B/12.9B, the balancing loss 2.8 and 1.0, the FNO layer 16,384 complex = 32,768 real + 1,056, linear-schedule alpha-bar_T = 0.132 at T = 200, 1/sqrt(0.001) = 31.6. All code snippets were executed: the PINN residual snippet reproduces Lab 4's initial losses (52.458 and 1.363 with torch.manual_seed(0)), the FNO layer runs at two grid sizes, nt_xent of collapsed embeddings gives log 511 exactly, and the MoE layer runs. The checker reports 0 errors.
changes: s12 Mixtral count: the plan says router and normalisation weights are 'about 1M'. The router alone is 32 x 8 x 4096 = 1.05M and the RMSNorm weights are about 0.27M (1.3M together). The text gives both figures separately.

s12 load-balancing minimum: the plan states the minimum as 1 at uniform routing without a proof. The text derives it with Cauchy-Schwarz for the case f_e ~ P_e (E sum P_e^2 >= (sum P_e)^2 = 1). With f and P free to differ, contrived routings can push E sum f_e P_e slightly below 1 (e.g. E = 3), so the bound is stated under that condition. The check's answer still says 'minimum 1, at uniform routing', as the plan does.
s12: the plan describes Jacobs et al. (1991) as 'a soft gate choosing among regressors'. The paper's experiments were vowel classification, so the text says 'expert networks' instead.

Added material that the plan does not contain: s9 times a classical baseline (SciPy solve_ivp RK45 at rtol 1e-8 gives a relative error of about 7e-9 in about 5 ms on this machine, against the PINN's 4e-4 after about 15 s); s12 adds the serving memory (46.7B x 2 bytes = 93 GB against 26 GB for 13B dense); s10 adds an FNO layer code sketch (PyTorch's numel counts a complex entry once and reports 17,440, against 33,824 real parameters).
